name: Chhit
ingredients: Fermented bamboo shoots (chhoyar), 200g, thoroughly washed and finely chopped
Split black gram (urad dal), 100g, soaked for 4 hours and drained
Red chili powder, 1 teaspoon (adjust to taste)
Black salt (kala namak), 1 teaspoon (or to taste)
Fresh coriander, a handful, chopped for garnish
instructions: 1. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until smoking lightly. Reduce heat and add cumin seeds; let them crackle. Add asafoetida and slit green chilies, sauté for 30 seconds.
2. Add the fermented bamboo shoots and turmeric. Stir-fry on medium heat for 5-7 minutes until the bamboo releases its aroma and begins to brown slightly.
3. Add the soaked urad dal and red chili powder. Mix well and cook for another 2 minutes.

4. Pour in 3 cups of warm water. Stir in black salt and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until the dal is tender and the bamboo shoots are soft, adding more water if needed for desired consistency.
5. Once cooked, garnish with julienned ginger and fresh coriander. For a richer flavor, drizzle with ghee just before serving. Serve steaming hot with steamed rice or warm flatbreads.
description: A slow-simmered, earthy embrace of fermented bamboo shoots and rustic lentils, redolent with spices that whisper of the Himalayan foothills.
